title: Opaque session credit resolver for late-arrival consumption claims
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We continue to see a class of sessions that cross shard boundaries or arrive after billing windows close. Those "opaque" sessions currently either get attributed incorrectly to a fallback tenant or are dropped from per-tenant charging, creating downstream invoice deltas and manual support tickets. This ticket implements a new idempotent resolution worker that deterministically computes per-tenant credit/charge adjustments for late-arriving or fragmented session traces and lands compact adjustment records into the canonical ledger.
goals: 1) Ensure deterministic, idempotent adjustments for late-arrival session segments. 2) Minimize per-tenant invoice noise by grouping small adjustments and providing confidence scores. 3) Provide observability for why an adjustment happened and provide a safe rollback path.
success_metrics:
- Percentage of late-arrival sessions resolved without manual support intervention < 4%
- Median resolution latency for late-arrivals < 15 minutes
- Adjustments that change final invoice totals by >1% limited to <0.5% of tenants
- No data duplication in ledger after 2 full release cycles
acceptance_criteria:
- Worker produces idempotent adjustment records keyed by (tenant_id, opaque_session_id, resolution_window)
- Adjustment records include a provenance blob (original shards, RSS checksum, confidence)
- New adjustment record types are understood by downstream invoicing/query services
- End-to-end integration test demonstrating: inject fragmented session traces, run resolver, ledger shows single compact adjustment, downstream invoice delta computed correctly
design_notes: High-level approach: build a stateless resolver service that consumes the session-segments topic and emits compact adjustment events to the ledger-writes topic. The resolver will: (a) maintain a small in-memory LRU for recent session fingerprints to dedupe within the resolution window, (b) compute attribution candidates using sequence-range overlap and heuristics (preferred tenant from strongest affinity score), (c) emit a single adjustment event that references the set of original segment ids and a deterministic UUID derived from tenant_id + session_fingerprint + window_start. Conflict resolution: ledger writer will perform upsert by deterministic UUID; consumer retries are safe because events are idempotent.
data_model_changes: New ledger record type: 'opaque_adjustment_v1' with fields (as stored in ledger rows): deterministic_id, tenant_id, claimed_tokens, original_segment_ids, confidence_score, window_start, created_by_job, source_checksums. Downstream query layer must index deterministic_id. Migration will include a compacting job to merge per-session micro-adjustments older than 30 days.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to worker pool with tenant-sampling (1% of tenants) for 48h
2) Increase sampling to 10% for 72h while monitoring metrics and sample invoices
3) Full rollout for new adjustment writes while keeping legacy fallback enabled for read-path until snapshot comparison passes
4) Run a 7-day differential pass (backfill) to resolve backlog with rate limit to avoid DB pressure
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for deterministic UUID generation and dedupe logic
- Integration test that replays synthetic fragmented sessions across shard boundaries and asserts a single ledger delta
- Chaos test: duplicate segment messages and validate idempotent outcome
- Load test to validate median processing latency under 10k late-arrivals/min
monitoring:
Create dashboards and alerts: 
- metric: resolver.adjustments.emitted (counts by tenant tier)
- metric: resolver.duplicates.detected (should trend to zero after dedupe improvements)
- metric: ledger.upsert_conflicts (errors)
- alert if adjustment rate increases >3x baseline or if median resolution latency > 30m
- provide a diagnostics endpoint that returns the last 10 resolved sessions for a tenant
open_questions: What's the TTL on the deterministic_id before we consider a session stale? (30d or 90d?)
Should we allow negative adjustments that affect already-closed invoices or only forward-looking credit notes?
Do we expose a customer-facing explanation for adjustments via the Console or only internal support tools?
